writing.exampleCaption: Classification checklist for Median from Two Heaps
writing.explanation:
A problem is a good match for Median from Two Heaps when it asks for online medians and percentile pivots. Here the concrete task is: Return medians after inserting 5, 2, 10, 4. The visible input `[5,2,10,4]` is an example, not a definition of the whole problem. Ask what operations the solution must support and what the input guarantees. Use it when only top-ranked candidates or repeated next-best extraction matters; sorting the entire stream may waste work. The right choice follows from those guarantees, not from a familiar noun in the prompt.

The decisive invariant is: Keep the lower half in a max-heap and upper half in a min-heap with sizes differing by at most one. Try to say why it applies to the task without quoting the implementation. Which fact becomes known after one update, and which possible answers remain? A heap keeps the current extremum accessible while new items arrive. Explain what belongs in the heap and what may be discarded. If that claim cannot be maintained on a legal input, the pattern is wrong or one of its preconditions is missing. A counterexample is more useful than a vague warning: change one property of the sample, trace the first two steps, and identify the exact claim that fails.

Compare costs before committing. The advertised bound is O(log n) insert · O(1) median · O(n) space; identify the operation responsible for it and the extra memory it needs. Then compare a straightforward alternative: a direct scan, full sort, or repeated recomputation may be easier but can pay for the same work many times. Do not choose the more elaborate method just because it has a famous name. For the sample, predict `5,3.5,5,4.5` and explain which part of the state lets the method reach that result.

When the prompt is ambiguous, ask about input size, ordering, duplicates, and required output format. Check an empty stream, k equal to zero or to the input length, duplicate priorities, and stale entries if deletion is lazy. Rust BinaryHeap is a max-heap; Reverse can express a min-heap. Keep the heap's ordering key separate from unrelated payload data. The Rust sketch can show a useful primitive without proving that the whole task is solved; connect each primitive to the requested output. You should be able to name a fitting case, a near miss, and the assumption separating them before writing the first line.
